verified: The Financial Times reported that Ukraine used drones fitted with mesh radios as airborne relay nodes to extend the communications link between operators and remotely piloted missiles during the Nov. 15–16 Kerch Strait Bridge strike, and that the operation did not rely on Starshield, the military version of Starlink; the Institute for the Study of War assessed that the strike collapsed one of the bridge’s two steel roadway arches. Telegraph and RBC Ukraine reports likewise describe a drone-relayed independent network, with RBC calling the drones “flying modems.”
unconfirmed: Whether Starlink or Starshield was actually disrupted during this strike—the FT headline says disruptions occurred “including during” the bridge attack, while the FT and Ars accounts say Ukraine deliberately avoided Starshield; also unverified are Russian claims that several hundred drones overwhelmed air defenses, the number, range and bandwidth of the relay drones, and any independent damage assessment beyond ISW’s.

verified: 据《金融时报》报道并经《每日电讯报》等媒体转述，乌克兰在 11 月 15 日至 16 日夜间的多轮无人机与导弹攻击中，使用了由搭载 mesh 电台（自组网电台）的无人机组成的中继网络，为远程操控的导弹和攻击无人机扩展通信链路；参与行动的部队刻意避开了 Starlink 的军用版本 Starshield。据战争研究所（ISW）11 月 17 日的战况更新，攻击造成刻赤海峡大桥两条承重钢拱之一垮塌。
unconfirmed: 上述战果与武器清单（包括乌方自研的 Flamingo 巡航导弹）主要依赖乌方及单一外部智库的说法，俄方仅称数百架无人机先行压制防空；中继无人机网络的具体规模、型号、链路带宽与抗干扰能力均未公开，也未见独立技术测试；“因 Starlink 反复中断才改用自建系统”的因果链条目前只有《金融时报》一方信源支撑。

titles.en: Ukraine fields relay drones to bypass Starlink in Kerch Bridge strike, FT reports
titles.zh: 乌克兰用无人机中继网络绕开星链限制，打击刻赤大桥
